page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs and 64 physical cores using the x86_64 architecture, driven by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in memory bandwidth for large blocks, reaching 209.21 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 269.5 GB/sec. Passmark database operations and extended instruction tests also register in the top 25% tier. Conversely, the instance exhibits weaker performance in LLM text generation, with text generation speeds for 135M and 7B models falling into the bottom 25% tier. Most other metrics, including single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, static web serving, and Redis SET operations, fall within the average range.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers high compute density relative to its memory footprint, making it a cost-efficient option for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory allocations or local NVMe storage. The absence of local storage means workloads must rely on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This server is appropriate for multi-threaded decompression, database operations, CPU-heavy extended instruction processing, and general compute-heavy tasks.
